sections.hypothesis: Trend-vol-target on BTC earns more per unit of risk if it steps into cash on days the regime model says the market is in its most volatile state.
sections.rationale: Economic reason: trend rules lose most in panicky, high-volatility markets that whip back and forth, where a trend signal turns too late. Outside evidence: Daniel and Moskowitz (Momentum Crashes, JFE 2016) find momentum crashes cluster in high-volatility panic states after declines, are partly forecastable, and that timing them roughly doubles momentum's Sharpe; that is cross-sectional momentum, so it is indirect evidence for this time-series rule. Not a rejected family: it is a filter on the one strategy on pursue. The regime model (kestrel.regimes, 3 states, fixed preset, filtered probabilities from monthly refits on the four years before) was built and fixed before this note; on BTC its volatile state averaged 85% annual volatility and lasted weeks. Risk: the crash brake, which sold on a single close, made trend-vol-target worse; this reacts to persistent states, but it may fail the same way. Written after trend-vol-target's 2020-25 and holdout results were seen.
sections.rules: Implementation trend-vol-target-regime at trend-vol-target's defaults, BTCUSDT 1d, 2021-05 to 2025-10 (every day has a regime state: the first fit needs four years of data from 2017-08), 330 USDT, costs from kestrel.toml. Two runs: kestrel backtest BTCUSDT --strategy trend-vol-target-regime --research <this note> --interval 1d --start 2021-05 --end 2025-10 --cash 330 (filter on), and the same with --param regime_filter=0 (the plain rule, the comparison).
sections.falsification: The filter is adopted only if, against the plain rule on the same period: (1) its Sharpe is higher; (2) its worst drawdown is no deeper; and (3) it fails no scorecard test the plain rule passes. Otherwise the note is rejected (with Luke's say-so) and trend-vol-target stays as it is. If adopted, it replaces nothing yet: it goes through the scorecard and joins paper trading as its own account. Run once.
sections.parameters: fast_days 20, mid_days 60, slow_days 120, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (trend-vol-target's defaults); regime_filter 1 (on) or 0 (comparison). The regime preset: 3 states, inputs log return and log 20-day volatility, 4-year training, monthly refits, seed 0.
sections.costs: About 22 bps a round trip. The filter adds a sale on entering the volatile state and a purchase on leaving it; it must earn those back. Two runs, two trials.
